newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bearish beneath $19.78.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bearish beneath $19.78.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+NYMEX crude oil futures are looking uncertain but traders and technical analysts are more inclined to be bearish.
+As long as the market remains under $19.78, August WTI crude is expected to head for lows in the mid-18 dollar range.
NYMEX crude oil futures are looking uncertain on Monday but traders and technical analysts say the market is likely to head for recent lows as long as prices stay beneath $19.78.

August WTI crude oil futures closed 11 cents a barrel firmer on Friday at $19.33. August unleaded gasoline ended the week 0.66 cents a gallon up at 59.26 while heating oil was 0.24 cents up at 52.35 cents a gallon.

"I would not be surprised to see it open unchanged or lower," said Tom Bentz at High Yield Analytics in New York. "As long as crude stays under $19.78 I will have to lean towards this thing trading down to its lows."
He said that an important number to watch was $18.65 a barrel, the recent low formed on the August contract chart on June 20.
Before that, however, he saw obstacles on the downwards path at $19.16 (Friday's low) and then at $19.07, the low point of the last week.
"That ($19.07) will be a critical level too," he said. "If we take that number out then we will be headed for the lows, in the mid-18s."
MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing the Market Profile technique, said in a daily report that support would be found at $19.20 and $19.05.
Bentz saw support for gasoline at 59.20, the focus of a lot of recent price action. Beneath that level lies 58 cents a gallon, he said.
